name: Mishael
overview: Mishael was a male Levite who played a role during the public reading of the Law as recorded in Nehemiah 8:4. He is noted for standing on Ezra's left hand while the Law was read, indicating a position of honor and involvement in this significant religious event. His Levite heritage is assumed based on his participation in this liturgical function.
namesAndTitles: The name Mishael means 'Who belongs to G-d [El]?' This proper name emphasizes a belonging or dedication to God, reflecting the spiritual identity of the individual mentioned in Nehemiah 8:4.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Mishael as a descendant of Levi, which aligns with his role in the religious assembly. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mishael's significance lies in his role during the public reading of the Law under Ezra's leadership, a key moment in Israel's spiritual restoration. His position beside Ezra symbolizes his involvement in upholding and transmitting God's covenant to the people. This event underscores the importance of the Levites in maintaining the worship and teaching of God's Word during the post-exilic period.
